mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, after a period of stagnation, indicates a nascent recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, despite the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Consistent week-on-week improvements in WORKPLACES mobility, if sustained for at least two consecutive weeks, will lead to increased weekday foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even if WORKPLACES continues to rise for two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in TRANSIT mobility signifies a shift away from home-centric activities towards out-of-home movement, directly boosting retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling and TRANSIT mobility rising concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in PARKS mobility in the most recent week, potentially driven by favorable weather, if it signals a broader public comfort with outdoor activities, will translate into increased engagement with other out-of-home retail and recreation options over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains high or increases, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite minor fluctuations, RESIDENTIAL mobility remains significantly elevated compared to baseline. This sustained preference for staying at home will continue to suppress overall out-of-home activity, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, even though RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility indicates a growing number of people moving around the city, which will directly lead to a short-term increase in incidental retail and recreation visits over the next week.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, returning to positive change, suggests a stabilization of essential out-of-home activities. This stabilization often precedes or accompanies a broader recovery in discretionary retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite some improvement in WORKPLACES mobility, the persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates that a significant portion of the population is still working from home or limiting out-of-home activities, which will constrain RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% while WORKPLACES is below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases significantly over the next 28 days, even with the described WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL mobility patterns.
